updates.name: Emily H. Stanley
updates.bio: Professor in the Department of Biology and the Center for Limnology at UW-Madison who studies how hydrology, geomorphology and carbon and nitrogen biogeochemistry shape streams and lakes, including methane and CO2 emissions from running waters. She has served as principal investigator of the North Temperate Lakes LTER and received ASLO's 2018 Hutchinson Award.
updates.research_interests: aquatic ecosystem ecology; biogeochemistry; carbon and nitrogen cycling; greenhouse gas dynamics; long-term ecosystem change; geomorphic and hydrologic influences on streams and lakes
updates.current_affiliation: Department of Biology and Center for Limnology, University of Wisconsin-Madison
updates.notes: Existing homepage https://limnology.wisc.edu/staff/stanley-emily/ is also 200 but carries only title/contact; switched to the Biology dept profile which has research text. Existing ORCID 0000-0003-4922-8121 checked: pub.orcid.org record name Emily Stanley, employment University of Wisconsin, Professor (consistent). NTL-LTER PI role evidence (2017 CFL blog): 'As Principal Investigator at the North Temperate Lakes Long-Term Ecological Research (NTL-LTER) site'. Lab site stanley.limnology.wisc.edu returned 403.
updates.evidence: As Principal Investigator at the North Temperate Lakes Long-Term Ecological Research (NTL-LTER) site

updates.name: Eric E. Knapp
updates.bio: Research ecologist with the USDA Forest Service Pacific Southwest Research Station, trained in genetics at the University of California (PhD 1992). His work examines how thinning, prescribed burning and fire exclusion affect California mixed-conifer and ponderosa pine forests, including long-term experiments such as the Variable Density Thinning Study and research on wildfire outcomes.
updates.research_interests: prescribed fire timing and effects; forest thinning and fuel treatment effectiveness against wildfire; fire history and legacy of fire exclusion in Sierra Nevada and Klamath forests; masticated fuels; home survival in wildfires
updates.current_affiliation: USDA Forest Service, Pacific Southwest Research Station
updates.notes: Old homepage research.fs.usda.gov/people/eric-knapp 404; new profile found at /about/people/eric.e.knapp (last updated June 2, 2026). ORCID shown on that profile and confirmed via pub.orcid.org/v3.0/0000-0002-6991-8157 (name Eric Knapp; employment USDA Forest Service, Research Ecologist). Blacks Mountain EF page (research.fs.usda.gov/psw/forestsandranges/locations/blacksmountain) lists Martin Ritchie as contact, not Knapp; Knapp co-authors Blacks Mountain-area treatment papers with Ritchie (e.g. Brodie et al. 2024) but no fetched page names him lead-PI of Blacks Mountain.
updates.evidence: Eric E. Knapp, PhD Research Ecologist Pacific Southwest Research Station 0000-0002-6991-8157

updates.name: Eric Terrill
updates.bio: Scripps Institution of Oceanography researcher in applied ocean science who directs the Marine Physical Laboratory and the Coastal Observing Research and Development Center (CORDC) at UC San Diego. His work spans ocean robotics and autonomous platforms, sensors and sonar, air-sea interaction and waves, and coastal circulation and pollution transport.
updates.research_interests: marine robotics and autonomous undersea systems; ocean sensors including sonar; ocean observing systems; air-sea interaction and surface waves; electromagnetic, electro-optic and acoustic propagation; coastal circulation, transport and pollution
updates.current_title: Director, Marine Physical Laboratory; Director, Coastal Observing Research and Development Center (CORDC)
updates.current_affiliation: Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UC San Diego
updates.notes: Title from scripps.ucsd.edu/profiles/eterrill: 'MPL Dir/Director of CORDC'. Existing ORCID 0000-0003-1807-8351 checked: pub.orcid.org name Eric Terrill, employment University of California, San Diego (consistent).

updates.name: Francis E. "Jack" Putz
updates.bio: Distinguished Professor of Biology at the University of Florida, where he has taught since 1982, with affiliate appointments in forest resources and natural resources programs. A Cornell PhD whose dissertation examined lianas in tropical forest dynamics, he works on tropical forestry, fire and restoration ecology, and conservation; he held Utrecht's Prince Bernhard chair 2004-2019.
updates.research_interests: conservation biology; tropical forestry; fire ecology; restoration ecology; economic botany; natural resource economics; plant ecology; plant biomechanics; lianas and tropical forest dynamics
updates.current_affiliation: Department of Biology, University of Florida
updates.notes: Old homepage biology.ufl.edu/people/francis-jack-putz/ 404; replaced with UF CLAS faculty site. Existing ORCID 0000-0003-0051-6675 checked: pub.orcid.org name Francis Putz, employment University of Florida, Distinguished Professor (consistent). No fetched page ties him to Ordway-Swisher lead-PI role.
updates.evidence: Distinguished Professor, Department of Biology, University of Florida, 2015-present

updates.name: Gaius R. Shaver
updates.bio: Emeritus Senior Scientist at the Marine Biological Laboratory's Ecosystems Center, with a Duke PhD in botany (1976). His research has centred on arctic tundra ecosystems, from early root growth and turnover studies at Barrow, Alaska, to plant nutrient responses and how warming and shrub expansion change tundra carbon storage.
updates.research_interests: arctic tundra plant and ecosystem ecology; root production and turnover in tundra; plant growth-form responses to nutrients and fertilization; arctic carbon storage and shrub expansion; global change ecology
updates.current_affiliation: The Ecosystems Center, Marine Biological Laboratory (University of Chicago)
updates.notes: Old homepage mbl.edu/research/scientists/gshaver/ 404; mbl.edu/user/104 redirects to the faculty-directory profile (200). Profile shows ORCID 0000-0002-6745-9989, matching the existing value; pub.orcid.org employment Marine Biological Laboratory from 1979. Ecosystems Center faculty page lists him under 'Distinguished and Emeritus Faculty' as 'Senior Scientist Emeritus' (status retired = emeritus).
updates.evidence: Gaius R. Shaver , Senior Scientist Emeritus

updates.name: Gary E. Belovsky
updates.bio: Professor Emeritus of Biological Sciences at the University of Notre Dame, where from 2001 he also directed the Notre Dame Environmental Research Center. A Harvard-trained ecologist, he combines theory with field experiments on foraging, herbivore population dynamics and nutrient cycling, through long-term studies at the National Bison Range, Montana, and Great Salt Lake, Utah.
updates.research_interests: foraging theory; herbivore population dynamics; interspecific competition; predator-prey dynamics; ecosystem nutrient cycling; grasshopper and grassland ecology (National Bison Range); Great Salt Lake ecosystem; conservation and pest management applications
updates.current_affiliation: Department of Biological Sciences, University of Notre Dame
updates.notes: ND profile title 'Professor Emeritus'; its biography still reads 'Gillen Director, Environmental Research Center ... 2001-Present' (stale), consistent with DB role former-director but no end date found.
